headline: Healthcare Leads a Split Tape as Genmab Rockets and F5 Sinks
body_html:
The market is tilting slightly negative at midday. Of the 539 stocks we track, 237 are higher and 300 are lower. Prices are not final and could change before the close.

Healthcare is the clear leader, up 1.11% as a group, with semiconductors a distant second at 0.39%. The other six groups are lower: energy is off 0.16%, materials 0.52%, consumer 0.54%, homebuilders 0.56%, software 0.65% and industrials 0.76%. Genmab is the standout mover, up 28.03%. Chemed (up 9.17%), Ensign Group (8.83%) and GE HealthCare (8.02%) add to the sector's strength. On the hardware side, Vertiv Holdings has gained 14.24% and Flex 7.31%.

The losers are just as dramatic. F5 is down 18.87%, Enphase Energy 16.12%, Landstar System 15.94% and CoStar Group 14.10%. Into the close, watch whether healthcare holds its lead, whether semiconductors stay positive while software lags, and whether these outsized single-stock swings narrow. The next session is Thursday, October 29.

briefs.headline: Genmab Surges More Than a Quarter
briefs.body: Genmab is the biggest gainer in our universe, up 28.03% at midday. The jump leads a healthcare group that is up 1.11%, the best of the eight sectors we track. Prices are still moving, so the final figure may differ.

briefs.headline: Data-Center Hardware Names Catch a Bid
briefs.body: Vertiv Holdings is up 14.24% and Flex has gained 7.31%, both well ahead of the broader market. Semiconductors are also positive, up 0.39%. The strength stands out against a session where more stocks are falling than rising.

briefs.headline: F5, Enphase and Landstar Take Heavy Losses
briefs.body: F5 has dropped 18.87%, Enphase Energy 16.12% and Landstar System 15.94%. CoStar Group is down 14.10%. The losses are spread across networking, solar, freight and real-estate data rather than concentrated in a single industry.

briefs.headline: Software and Industrials Trail the Field
briefs.body: Industrials are the weakest group at midday, down 0.76%, with software close behind at 0.65%. Homebuilders, consumer and materials are each down roughly half a percent. Only healthcare and semiconductors are in positive territory.

briefs.headline: Mega-Cap Tech Group Is Reportedly Pulling Apart
briefs.body: Market commentary today says the once tightly linked group of giant technology stocks is moving less in unison. That leaves investors to sort leaders from laggards stock by stock. The split within technology on our tape fits that view, with semiconductors up and software down.

briefs.headline: Middle East Tensions Linger in the Background
briefs.body: Reports say Iran sees nothing acceptable in the latest mediation effort to end the war. Separately, Houthi forces struck an airport in Yemen after warning of an evacuation. Energy is down 0.16% at midday, a modest move so far.
